classification.difficultyReason: Complete two familiar cases of the centre/circumference theorem using explicitly supplied intermediate goals, isosceles radii and exterior-angle sums or differences. Four short linked property deductions are scaffolded; no independent auxiliary construction or novel proof strategy is required.

content.prompt:
Prove that: An angle at the centre subtended by an arc is twice an angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.

We proved Case 1 of this and noted Case 4 follows in the same manner. We pointed out that there are two other cases to consider.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Using the diagram to the right:

spec.description: Diameter AP, chord PB and dashed radius OB; beta at B and unlabelled angle arcs at P and O.

answer.short: $\angle APB=\beta$, by equal base angles in $\triangle OPB$.
answer.worked:
$OP=OB$ because they are radii, so $\triangle OPB$ is isosceles and $\angle OPB=\angle PBO=\beta$.

Since $A,O,P$ are collinear, $\angle APB=\angle OPB=\beta$.

answer.short: $\angle AOB=2\beta$, by the exterior-angle theorem in $\triangle OPB$.
answer.worked:
$\angle AOB$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle OPB$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=\angle OPB+\angle PBO\\\angle AOB&=\beta+\beta\\\angle AOB&=2\beta.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Using the diagram to the right:

spec.description: Chords AP and PB, dashed OA, OB and OP extended through O towards X; alpha uses an external leader.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source labels and angle arcs.

answer.short:
$\angle APB=\beta-\alpha$.

Subtract the base angles obtained from equal radii.
answer.worked:
$OA=OP$, so $\angle APO=\angle OAP=\alpha$.

$OB=OP$, so $\angle OPB=\angle PBO=\beta$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle APB&=\angle OPB-\angle OPA\\\angle APB&=\beta-\alpha.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\angle AOB=2(\beta-\alpha)=2\angle APB$.

Subtract the exterior angles at $O$.
answer.worked:
Since $PO$ is produced to $X$, the exterior-angle theorem gives $\angle XOB=2\beta$ in $\triangle OPB$ and $\angle XOA=2\alpha$ in $\triangle OPA$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=\angle XOB-\angle XOA\\\angle AOB&=2\beta-2\alpha\\\angle AOB&=2(\beta-\alpha)\\\angle AOB&=2\angle APB.\end{align*}$$
